conclusion: Heterozygous carrier of the SIRT6 rs117385980 T allele. Two small, underpowered cohort studies independently report this allele depleted among the longest-lived, and they agree on the direction of the effect. Neither reaches statistical significance, neither measured lifespan directly, and the magnitude is not established. A research-grade trend, not an individual prediction.
negatives: In the Iranian cohort the same allele was more frequent among robust (non-frail) participants than among the frail, the opposite direction to its depletion at advanced age. The authors call this a diverse effect and raise antagonistic pleiotropy as one possible explanation; it is unexplained.

conclusion: Two copies of the reference C allele at SIRT6 rs117385980. The minor T allele that the longevity studies report is absent. This is the common genotype in every population reported by the source papers, and the trend those papers describe in its favour was not statistically significant, so no lifespan advantage is asserted for it here: the weight is an explicit zero rather than a blank. A no-call at this position is not this result and must not be reported as one.

Two copies of the SIRT6 rs117385980 T allele. Neither source study observed this genotype in any participant: both cohorts carried the T allele only in heterozygous form, and population databases record it as rare. Nothing in this module's evidence base speaks to it, so no direction, no significance and no weight are asserted. Any inference from the heterozygous finding to this genotype would be the reader's own, not the cited studies'.
